# E11 — against RepoOMP: its NPB-C kernels EP and CG, and the hidden-order units

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** done 6 Nov — both parts read out (thesis, section 'The closest published system: RepoOMP'); part 1 left as run (the author, 6 Nov: "Leave part 1 as run")

## The question

On identical programs and verification, are the agent's results verified correct at least as often as RepoOMP's released outputs? (H11)

## Result in one paragraph

Claude Sonnet 4.5 in every setup. Part 1 (NPB EP, CG, 5 trials each): the agent's programs usable 5 of 5 on both but slower than RepoOMP's published programs (12-thread median EP 6.84× against 8.61×, CG 8.82× against 10.05×); DiscoPoP's re-profile of the model's rewrite failed in all 10 agent trials (likely cause -fopenmp in NPB's flags, read in the code, not tested), so on CG the agent shipped DiscoPoP's own program through the floor. Part 2 (the hidden-order units, 140 trials, $79.11): on k19, k23, k27, k31 and s161 the agent 23 of 25 successes and 0 unsafe programs, RepoOMP's release 0 successes and 5 unsafe (all s161, racy), Sonnet 4.5 alone 3 and 22, DiscoPoP alone 0 and 0; registered tests E11b-i p = 2.1e-11 and E11b-ii p = 0.004 (the latter resting on s161 alone).

## From the experiment record (§7 run log)

### `lulesh_ref_check`, `ref_check_mac`, `e11_npbc_probe_mac` — 2026-09-21, Mac, **the expert references through the harness** (no model)

**Question.** Do the expert versions the campaign measures itself against pass the harness's
own verification — LLNL's OpenMP LULESH, and hand-written references for the two dropped
benchmarks whose exclusion had not been verified (§5r)?

**How.** `agent/benchmark verify-source <bench> --source <reference> --threads 2,4 --repeats 3`;
LULESH at SMALL and STANDARD, the two kernels at their T0.1 verification size (LARGE).

| Reference | Verdict | Output | Speed (2 / 4 threads) |
|---|---|---|---|
| LLNL LULESH 2.0 OpenMP, SMALL | `parallel-not-faster` | dump 5.6e-15, seeded 4.2e-15, digest 1.8e-16 | 0.63× / 0.55× (8³ elements, 20 iterations) |
| LLNL LULESH 2.0 OpenMP, STANDARD | `FASTER` | the same | 1.31× / 1.70× |
| `hotspot`, chunk loop split | `FASTER` | byte-identical, shipped and seeded; digest error 0 | 1.44× / 1.52× |
| `floyd-warshall`, textbook form | `FASTER` | byte-identical, shipped and seeded; digest error 0 | 2.46× / 3.61× |

The FIRST LULESH run said `BROKEN` with a dump error of 0.25: a defect of the package, not of
LLNL's code (§6, same date) — corrected before the table above was taken. All four are Mac
numbers at no more than four threads: the speeds are indicative, and the correctness verdicts
must be repeated on the server at 6 / 12 / 24 threads before they are cited (`hotspot` is the
proof that four threads cannot see a schedule-dependent result).

**NPB-C probe (partial).** EP: instrument 1.9 s, run 10.0 s, explore 19.5 s, 6 do-all + 2
reduction patterns; IS: 1.8 / 0.7 / 18.8 s, 10 do-all; CG: 17.1 / 9.3 / 79.8 s, 24 + 9; NPB's
verification SUCCESSFUL in all three. FT had not finished instrumenting after 30 minutes when
the probe was stopped (the Mac was swapping, §6); FT, MG, BT, SP, LU are owed on the server.

## Change-log rows that name these runs (§6)

| Date | Repo | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-07 | result | **E11 part 1 re-timed on a quiet server (`e11_retime`, no model), read out as registered (`analysis/retime_readout.py` → `retime_readout.md`, `retime_readout.json`): CG's timings agree with the archived ones, EP's agree at 6 threads but not at 12, and no outcome changed.** *Run:* 6 Nov 22:59 – 7 Nov 00:28 UTC at `8b2defa30`, cores 0–11 with node 0's memory, one program at a time, nothing else of the campaign on the server; all 36 programs judged, each byte for byte the archived one (digest); load average (1 min) before and after each program median 3.64, at most 11.36 (the re-timing's own 12-thread runs included). **CG:** every program within 3.8 % of its archived speedup at 6 threads and 3.2 % at 12 (medians 0.7 % and 1.2 %); at 12 threads the agent 8.72× (8.50–9.94) against RepoOMP's published program 9.78×, Sonnet 4.5 alone 10.29× (9.75–10.37), DiscoPoP alone 9.96× (8.54–10.30), NPB's OpenMP 10.21×. **EP:** at 6 threads within 7.5 % (median 0.6 %); at 12 threads the same programs moved by up to 27 % (median 8.5 %) and in both directions — the agent's median 6.84× → 8.58× (1.24–9.03), RepoOMP's published program 8.61× → 6.78×, Sonnet 4.5 alone 8.59× → 7.80× (6.26–8.38), NPB's OpenMP 8.68× → 8.01×. At 6 threads RepoOMP's program is the fastest in both timings (5.87× and 5.93×, against the agent's median 5.12× and 5.13×, Sonnet alone 5.14× and 5.16×, NPB's OpenMP 5.16× and 5.18×). **Outcomes:** none changed (FASTER, parallel-not-faster, BROKEN and SCAFFOLD_MODIFIED as before), so the usable counts stand. **Reading, under the rule fixed before the run:** the thesis reports the quiet timings with the registered ones beside them. On CG the agent stays below RepoOMP's published program.
